description: Names University Heights 3 neighbourhood 'Sunrise'.
Adds 'Hawthorn' and 'Sunrise' to city's master name list.

chips.text: Approved
5 for, 0 against
Councillor Parker praised the engagement process, stating it was money well spent.
The naming process involved targeted community engagement, an exception to existing policy.
Elders and youth advocated for 'Sunrise' due to its traditional and ceremonial significance.
The naming process prioritized Indigenous community engagement for inclusive names.
Administration will present revised naming policy updates within several months.

speakers.name: Nora Cummings
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: University Heights 3 Neighbourhood
said: Elders and youth chose "Sunrise" for its traditional meaning.
Hopes council honors indigenous people's decision for the name.
Indigenous people should have a say in naming land.

segments.title: Elder's Presentation on Sunrise Name
description: Elder Norah Cummings presented the name "Sunrise" for the new neighborhood.
The name was chosen through a process involving elders and young people.
"Sunrise" reflects traditional Indigenous ways of life and teachings.
The name is intended to be displayed in multiple languages.

chips.text: Elders and young people chose 'Sunrise' for its traditional significance.
Name chosen through Indigenous community engagement and ceremonial practices.

segments.title: Administration Report on Naming Policy and UH3
description: Administration presented a history of the Civic Naming Committee and current policy.
The place identity framework was approved but policy updates are outstanding.
Targeted engagement led to "Sunrise" as the preferred name for UH3.
Recommendations include adding "Hawthorne" and "Sunrise" to the master list.

chips.text: New place identity framework approved to guide future naming processes.
Policy revisions are underway to align with the new place identity framework.

segments.title: Committee Questions on Hawthorne and Future Naming
description: Committee inquired about the cultural significance and future use of the "Hawthorne" name.
"Hawthorne" is a traditional medicine suitable for park areas.
Saskatoon Land supports the "Sunrise" name and plans to incorporate Indigenous references.
Future developments will include opportunities for Indigenous street and park names.

chips.text: Hawthorne name has ceremonial significance for Indigenous community, suitable for parks.
Saskatoon Land will incorporate Indigenous references on signs and for street/park names.

segments.title: Chair's Inquiry on Policy, Costs, and Developer Input
description: The committee's request for community engagement was an exception to current policy.
The targeted engagement cost approximately $16,000, primarily for honorariums.
Future policy updates will balance developer requests with community engagement.
The legacy naming project funded the engagement process.

chips.text: $16,000 spent on targeted community engagement, mainly for honorariums.
Future engagement processes may require committee approval as policy exceptions.

segments.title: Committee Reflections and Policy Concerns
description: Councillor Parker praised the unique engagement process as money well spent.
Chair cautioned against discarding previous work on the naming list and policy.
Chair expressed concern about future budget and staff time for the new process.
Chair recommended the policy discussion go to the full City Council.

chips.text: Councillor Parker praised staff for navigating an 'outside the norm' process.
Chair recommended full council discussion on policy at General Policy Committee.

segments.title: Vote on Naming Recommendations
description: The committee voted on the four recommendations from administration.
Recommendations included adding "Hawthorne" and "Sunrise" to the master list.
"Sunrise" was approved as the name for University Heights 3 neighborhood.
The report will be forwarded to City Council for information.

chips.text: Recommendations to add names and apply 'Sunrise' to UH3 were carried.
Motion carried with no opposition.
